profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 in Sterling offers 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, equivalent to roughly 275 racks at typical AI training density, but ranks 26th among Virginia facilities with published capacity and represents less than 1% of the state's disclosed total.

Virginia maps 330 data centers, yet only 25 publish capacity figures. This fragmentation means the state's true infrastructure base remains largely opaque. CyrusOne NVA4's published 11 MW places it outside Virginia's top tier by disclosed power, though the 305 unmapped or unpublished facilities could contain larger campuses that would reshape the ranking.

The facility's design emphasizes network connectivity over power density. Multiple metro and long-haul circuits address data movement constraints for distributed workloads, suggesting a role in inference or specialized compute rather than centralized training. An 11 MW facility alone cannot sustain frontier model development, which demands orders of magnitude more power concentrated in single locations.

The data does not disclose actual power draw, PUE efficiency, cooling capacity, or whether the facility has been built out to its 11 MW limit. It also does not indicate whether CyrusOne operates other Virginia campuses that would combine into a more significant regional footprint for AI workloads. Without visibility into Virginia's 305 unpublished facilities, assessments of the state's role in AI infrastructure scaling remain incomplete.
